# Reference

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Remove the roof basket, then locate and remove four bolts attaching it to the roof. [t719]

Remove the plastic light covers to access the bulb housing for a 9005 (HB3). [t719]

Install the correct 9005 bulbs into the housing. [t719]

[Partial] Replace the plastic covers over the lights with a bulb type of 9005. [t719]

[Partial] Turn on the high beams using a bulb type of 9005. [t719]

Take the plastic covers off and use a 9005 bulb. [t719]

Activate the Off Road lamp switch and use a 9005 bulb. [t719]

Remove the entire air dam from the vehicle if needed. [t719]

Adjust the lights using an adjustment screw located in a hole on the housing. [t719]

[Partial] Swap the fog lights and off-road lamps to 20,000LM bulbs. [t719]

[Partial] Install 9007 bulbs with a brightness of 20,000LM in the headlight assemblies. [t719]

Access the bottom bulb on the front bumper by removing the whole headlight assembly. [t719]

[Partial] Remove the relay box from behind the battery and install new open barrel terminals into its sockets. [t478]

Determine that Bank 1 is located on the passenger side cylinder. [t492]

Note that the primary catalytic converter uses studs for installation. [t492]

[Partial] Check if the secondary catalytic converter is necessary based on local emissions testing. [t492]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Locate the relay box situated just behind the battery and in front of the IPDM box.
2. Open the box by pressing release tabs on both sides to separate it into two halves.
3. Remove the vehicle's battery to relieve electrical load during disassembly.
4. Use a 10mm socket with an extension to remove the screw securing the relay box assembly.
5. Stab a small flathead screwdriver behind the center of the box to release the tab holding it to the IPDM.
6. Gently pull and rotate the upper half up toward the engine until wires loosen enough for clearance.
7. [Partial] Release the front tabs which are easier to manipulate than the rear ones.
8. Push inward on the rear side tabs simultaneously while lifting the whole unit off at once.
9. Use a seal pick or flat screwdriver to assist if necessary without breaking components.
10. [Partial] Press a small release tab on an individual relay socket from inside the box to remove it.
11. Insert new open barrel terminals into sockets by pushing them in until the tapered part hits the locking tab and clicks.
12. Run the assembled upper half of the relay box back over the installed sockets, ensuring correct orientation.
13. [Partial] Snap the two halves together securely around the IPDM mounting point.
14. Reinsert the screw to secure the assembly against the IPDM box.
15. [Partial] Reinstall the battery and test electrical connections.

_Procedure reported by [t478]. Photos of this job are in the source: <https://www.xterranation.org/index.php?threads/how-to-crack-open-the-relay-box-and-replace-relay-sockets.9975/>_

## Specifications

- **Attachment point**: 4 bolts on the leading edge that attach directly to the roof [t719] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Bolt count**: 1 each on either side at the back part where it attaches to the roof rack [t719] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Brightness**: 20,000LM [t719] ([Partial] [Unverified] single report)
- **Bulb brightness**: 20,000LM [t719] ([Unverified] single report)
- **Bulb type**: DISPUTED, sources disagree: 9005 (HB3) [t719]; 9007 [t719]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Note the two unused slots if planning a retrofit installation. [t478]
- Ensure bare wire ends go over the smaller crimping area of the tool before crimping insulation around them. [t478]
- Label wires after installing new sockets to avoid confusion later. [t478]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Forcing rear tabs without pushing inward first, risking breakage. [t478]
- [Partial] Dropping components during disassembly due to lack of patience or tools like a seal pick. [t478]
